items.title: Judges in malpractice case received $32,500 in contributions from Baker Botts and counsel
items.summary: Houston’s 14th Court of Appeals upheld a confidential arbitration award favoring Baker Botts after the firm and lead counsel made at least $32,500 in campaign contributions to five judges connected to the matter, including $6,500 to Justice Ken Wise while the appeal was pending. Contributions alone do not establish wrongdoing. Timing raises disclosure, recusal, and appearance questions. Trial judge Phillips previously received an SCJC public warning in an unrelated disclosure matter.
items.eve_read: The dates sit next to a live appeal. That is an appearance question: disclosure, recusal, and whether the other side was told. Money on a docket is not a finding of bribery. It is a reason to look.

items.title: Recusal attempt fails in Dallas civil case involving Cowboys owner Jerry Jones
items.summary: Former appellate judge Erin Nowell denied a recusal motion against State District Judge Aiesha Redmond in a civil case alleging misconduct by Jerry Jones. Ruling: movant did not show bias; Texas rules do not allow recusal based solely on a judge’s prior rulings. Plaintiff’s counsel filed a further recusal motion the next day.
items.eve_read: Recusal is the public’s first lever when a bench looks captured. A denial on ‘rulings only’ is legally ordinary. The follow-up motion about staff contact with a commentator is the thread to keep watching — sourced, not speculated.
